[Most of my theory work starts as a simulation. The models from my papers are open source, mostly in Python, so you can check the assumptions, rerun the results, or build on them.]{.lede}

::: {.sect}
[Models from papers]{.label}

::: {.body}
::: {.item}
[[deliberation](https://github.com/helgeklapper/deliberation)]{.repo-id}

[Agents with partial information deliberate over a social network and then vote. Parameters set group size, information quality, network density, and the strength of conformity pressure, and a built-in sweep compares any two of them.]{.desc}

[Python · NumPy, NetworkX · for Klapper, Maciejovsky, Puranam & Reitzig (2026), *Strategic Organization*]{.meta}
:::

::: {.item}
[[nearmiss](https://github.com/helgeklapper/nearmiss)]{.repo-id}

[Organizational learning model with near misses.]{.desc}

[Python · for working paper with J. Madiedo]{.meta}
:::

::: {.item}
[[socialinfluence](https://github.com/helgeklapper/socialinfluence)]{.repo-id}

[Simulates information sharing and voting in a group.]{.desc}

[Python]{.meta}

[Replications for teaching]{.label}

::: {.item}
[[Organizational-Decision-Making](https://github.com/helgeklapper/Organizational-Decision-Making)]{.repo-id}

[A replication of Csaszar & Eggers (2013), *Management Science*. The paper solves its integrals numerically; this version simulates the same decision structures with random draws, which makes it easier to follow in class.]{.desc}

[Python · written for teaching]{.meta}
